sentences.text:
On The 12th Of November, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 43504 of 2024
 Aakash
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Kuldeep Singh Rajpoot - Advocate for applicant.
 Ms. Ranjana Agnihotri - Dy. Government Advocate for State.
None for the respondent No.2.
ORDER This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita).

He is in custody since 22.08.2024 in connection with Crime No.535/2024 registered at P.S.- Kotwali, Narmadapuram District Narmadapuram, (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376, 376(3) of IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, 2012. .
3. Prosecution story in brief is that applicant has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix.

Therefore, aforesaid offences were registered against applicant.
4.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is in custody since 22.08.2024.
Proseuctrix is a consenting party.
There is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
Charge-sheet has been filed and trial will take NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55607 2 MCRC-43504-2024 considerable time.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application on the ground that at the time of incident, age of the prosecutrix was below 16 years.
Applicant took the minor prosecutrix without consent of her parents and committed sexual intercourse with her.
DNA report is also found positive.
In view of above, he prayed for dismissal of this bail application.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case- diary.

7. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances, age of prosecutrix and seriousness of offence, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
8.
Accordingly, present bail application stands dismissed.
